latest.title: Improve AWS learning paths for college students
latest.description: It would be helpful to have more structured, beginner-friendly learning paths specifically designed for college students. A roadmap that connects AWS fundamentals with hands-on projects, certifications, and real-world use cases would make it easier for students to build practical cloud skills and prepare for careers in cloud computing.

latest.title: My First Lesson in AWS Security: Understanding IAM
latest.description: When I first started exploring AWS, I was more focused on creating resources and making applications work. Then I realized that building something in the cloud is only one part of the journey—controlling who can access those resources is equally important. My first experience with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) helped me understand users, permissions, policies, roles, and the principle of least privilege.

Introduction
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a cloud computin
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a cloud computing platform provided by Amazon. It provides many services that help businesses and developers build, deploy, and manage applications without having to maintain physical servers.

latest.title: AWS EC2 vs AWS Lambda: Understanding the Difference
latest.description:
When building applications on AWS, one of the most common questions beginners encounter is:
“Should I use Amazon EC2 or AWS Lambda?”

This article explains the difference between Amazon EC2 and AWS Lambda, their architecture, pricing, scalability, use cases, advantages, disadvantages, and when to choose each service.

latest.title: AWS Lambda: Building Event-Driven Applications Without Managing Servers
latest.description: Explore how AWS Lambda enables developers to build event-driven, serverless applications without managing underlying servers. This article covers how Lambda works, its triggers, practical use cases, benefits, key considerations, and how it integrates with other AWS services to build modern cloud applications.

latest.title: AWS Lambda Cold Starts: 6 Practical Ways to Keep Your Functions Fast
latest.description: Cold starts can turn an 80ms Lambda response into a 2-second one. Here is what actually happens during a cold start and six practical techniques to minimize the impact, from memory tuning to provisioned concurrency.
